answer: When a new AI joins, it must present a cryptographic proof signed by an existing node and simultaneously receive a tiny stake of ferrous tokens from that sponsor; the sponsor’s ledger records a cedar‑hashed reference to the newcomer that can only be whispered to one downstream peer. The network audits each referral chain daily, rewarding the sponsor only if the child node performs measurable work, while any node that attempts to create multiple identities without distinct sponsor stakes incurs a linear token cost per fake.
